{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABYtVh_Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhCSTVw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 27, "title": "Expand cartridge mapper compatibility with SRAM-backed MegaROMs and special ROM layouts", "body": "## Problem

The emulator currently accepts Plain, ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami Standard, and Konami SCC cartridges, but has no cartridge SRAM and assumes power-of-two bank-switched ROM sizes. Some MSX1/MSX2 cartridge games use SRAM-backed ASCII mappers or different bank layouts, and their ROMs either fail to load, execute with incorrect banking, or cannot save progress. The current mapper detector also cannot identify these variants.

The goal is to **increase the number of MSX1/MSX2 cartridge ROMs that can actually run**, including save-capable cartridges, without relying on proprietary game ROMs, game-specific hacks, or unsafe "Auto" guesses.

## Expected outcome

Extend the current Rust core, Wasm interface, and browser's `Cartridge mapper` selection with these **specific documented families**:

1. **ASCII8 with SRAM**, including the standard documented 2 KiB and 8 KiB SRAM variants (`ASCII8SRAM2` / `ASCII8SRAM8`).
2. **ASCII16 with SRAM**, including the standard documented 2 KiB and 8 KiB SRAM variants (`ASCII16SRAM2` / `ASCII16SRAM8`).
3. **R-Type's special 384 KiB ROM layout**, whose fixed/initial bank mapping and non-power-of-two size differ from existing ASCII16 behavior.

Implement the documented bank/SRAM selection bits, read/write visibility and mirroring **per mapper variant**, not as a generic writeable window. Users should be able to play compatible cartridges and retain their SRAM save data locally across sessions. Preserve plain ROMs, existing MegaROMs, classic SCC sound, the built-in demos, C-BIOS, Weave BASIC and automatic MSX2-first browser startup.

This Issue covers **these initial additional families**, not all historical MSX mapper variants, disk/tape, MSX2+, SCC+ or a general-purpose multi-cartridge architecture. The Konami Game Master 2 add-on typically requires a second cartridge slot; treat that as future work rather than silently claiming support in the current single-cartridge architecture.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository: `takahirox/msx-rust`; `main` was `dcebd6bb4402` when drafted.
- `crates/msx-core/src/cartridge.rs` currently defines only `Mapper::{Auto,Plain,Ascii8,Ascii16,Konami,KonamiScc}`; mapper validation rejects non-power-of-two MegaROM lengths and `Mapping` has no SRAM storage. `crates/msx-core/src/cartridge/detect.rs` only infers existing four MegaROM families.
- `crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs` owns the cartridge bus, mapping, memory and firmware reset; `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs` exposes raw mapper values to `web/app.js` / the mapper selector in `web/index.html`. Changes must keep both layers consistent, preserve active sessions on failed imports, and avoid unbounded copies of uploaded ROMs.
- The built-in BIOS policy from #19, the licensed Demo ROMs from #21, classic SCC audio from #23, and MSX2-first startup from #25 are existing regression requirements.
- Independent technical references for the selected mapper families:
  - https://www.msx.org/wiki/MegaROM_Mappers (ASCII SRAM bank-select variants and special layouts)
  - https://www.msx.org/wiki/ROM_mappers (ASCII SRAM variant notes; R-Type bank mapping)
  - https://openmsx.org/manual/faq (SRAM saves and the difference between embedded cartridge SRAM and Game Master 2)
- Do not copy another emulator's implementation code. Derive behavior from documented hardware registers and independently authored executable fixtures.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Mapper implementation and correctness

- [ ] Implement explicit mapper IDs and correct memory behavior for `ASCII8SRAM2`, `ASCII8SRAM8`, `ASCII16SRAM2`, `ASCII16SRAM8` and the `R-Type` 384 KiB special layout. Verify the actual address decoding, reset bank selection, appropriate SRAM select bits, ROM/SRAM mirroring and protection, and bank wrapping/physical size limits for **each** supported variant against documented hardware. Do not treat all SRAM-backed ASCII games as having identical address or select bits.
- [ ] Wire SRAM through the actual selected cartridge slot and Z80 read/write path. SRAM reads/writes should be visible only through selected bank windows and only in SRAM mode; ROM remains protected, and writes in unmapped slots must not alter SRAM or mapper registers.
- [ ] Support R-Type's documented initial/fixed bank and its **384 KiB non-power-of-two** ROM image without weakening size and header validation for ordinary mappers. Unsupported partial/overlarge or malformed images must still be rejected with specific explanations.
- [ ] Preserve mapper and SRAM semantics on Reset, cartridge replacement, Eject, model change, and manual/automatic firmware selection. Reset must reset mapper bank registers **without erasing battery-backed SRAM**. SRAM belongs to the individual cartridge, not the machine, while other cartridges must never inherit its content.
- [ ] Failed, ambiguous or out-of-memory ROM imports must be atomic: keep the existing machine model, firmware, active cartridge, mapper registers and unsaved SRAM intact. Never allocate or commit save data before the incoming cartridge is fully validated.
- [ ] Extend the existing manual mapper selection and raw Wasm ABI without silently renumbering existing public mapper values. Automatic detection may select a new mapper only with genuinely discriminating evidence; otherwise present a clear manual choice, especially because ROM header/size alone usually cannot prove SRAM hardware. Document supported hardware limits and uncertainty rather than inventing compatibility.

### Saving and restoring SRAM

- [ ] Provide **durable local save/restore** for supported battery-backed cartridge SRAM across a browser reload or revisit (e.g., browser-local storage or an explicit, functioning save export/import workflow). Use a stable per-ROM identity derived from local ROM bytes and selected mapper; validate restored save size/version and reject incorrect or corrupted data without damaging the current game. Do not persist original game ROM images or send them to a server.
- [ ] Make SRAM retention, reset and optional deletion/import/export behavior understandable in the browser UI without cluttering the primary screen. Avoid silent overwrites or cross-game save collisions when switching demos, changing mapper variants or importing similarly named ROMs.
- [ ] Ensure save storage failures (permissions/quota/corrupt data) are nonfatal and accurately reported, and local cartridge execution remains possible without persistence.

### Automated coverage, documentation and deployment

- [ ] Add independently authored ROM fixtures for each new mapper variant that execute real Z80 code, switch banks, read/write SRAM, demonstrate save restoration and exercise the special R-Type layout; inspect actual emulated memory and observable output. No proprietary or commercial cartridge bytes are permitted.
- [ ] Add Rust unit/integration tests for each mapper's register decoding, SRAM size/select/readback, writable windows, bank mirrors, reset vs retention, save-data isolation and validation, firmware/slot interactions, failed imports and existing mapper/SCC regressions.
- [ ] Add Playwright browser/Wasm tests under both `/` and `/msx-rust/` that import original fixtures using the real ROM picker, choose all new manual mapper types, execute a bank-switched program, write SRAM, reload/revisit and restore its values, then switch to another ROM without leaking the save. Check invalid/corrupted save and failed import behavior. Preserve MSX1/MSX2 BASIC, C-BIOS boot, existing curated Demo ROMs, SCC audio, keyboard/video, and GitHub Pages-relative asset behavior.
- [ ] Update README, mapper documentation, advanced-system help, supported-ROM format and saving guidance, including explicit non-support for additional specialized cartridges / Game Master 2's second-slot use. Avoid implying universal ROM or save-game compatibility.
- [ ] Run and accurately report `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test`, and any relevant save-storage validations. Complete the normal English Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → revision → merge workflow. All pre-merge checks must be executable by AI; do not require original commercial game ROMs, physical MSX hardware, manual gameplay or subjective owner approval.

## Optional validation

The owner may later try lawfully obtained games that use the newly supported SRAM mappers or the R-Type layout, including in-game save/load, and report differences as separate Issues. This is not a pre-merge requirement.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] After merge and successful GitHub Pages publication, verify the **live** https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ build runs independently authored fixtures for at least one ASCII SRAM mapper and the R-Type mapper through the published Wasm, with visible execution; verify that a cartridge SRAM save can be recovered after a fresh page load, and confirm the existing MSX2 default/BASIC and demo-ROM flows remain usable. Record deployment commit, Actions run, tested URLs and results. This is a **post-merge** check, not a condition for merging; file a separate Issue for any deployed-site failure.
